120726.sol: Prolonged heating with HI results in the formation of n-hexane, which suggests that all six carbon atoms are linked in a straight chain.

120842.subject: Chemistry

options: (A) is true, (R) is true and (R) is the correct explanation for (A)
(A) is true, (R) is true but (R) is not the correct explanation for (A)
120842.sol: In aqueous solution, the carboxyl group can lose a proton and amino group can accept a proton, giving rise to a dipolar ion known as zwitter ion. This is neutral but contains both positive and negative charges. In zwitter ionic form, amino acids show amphoteric behaviour as they react both with acids and bases. Proline has a secondary amine group

121332.subject: Botany
121332.text: What is the phase called when an intervening dikaryotic stage occurs?
121332.sol: When a fungus reproduces sexually, two haploid hyphae of compatible mating types come together and fuse. In some fungi the fusion of two haploid cells immediately results in diploid cells (2n). However, in other fungi (ascomycetes and basidiomycetes), an interveningdikaryotic stage (n + n, i.e., two nuclei per cell) occurs; such a condition is called a dikaryon and the phase is called dikaryophase of fungus. Later, the parental nuclei fuse and the cells become diploid. The fungi form fruiting bodies in which reduct

121637.subject: Botany
121637.text: Which motile-stage of protozoans is helpful in feeding?
121637.sol: Pseudopodium is helpful in the feeding of protozoans. It is a temporary cytoplasm-filled projection of a eukaryotic cell membrane. It can be used for motility or for ingesting nutrients or other particulate matter.

122350.subject: Botany
122350.text: Which Phylum does this organism belong to?

122663.subject: Botany
122663.sol: Chondrichthyes is one of the classes of super-class-Pisces, sub-phylum-Vertebrata and phylum-Chordata. The members of class-Chondrichthyes are marine animals with streamlined body and have cartilaginous endoskeleton. Mouth is located ventrally. The skin is tough, containing minute placoid scales. The teeth aremodified placoid scales which are backwardly directed, e.g., Dog fish (Scoliodon), saw fish (Pristis), great white shark (Carcharodon), sting ray (Trygon), etc.

122752.subject: Botany
122752.text: Can there be a variation in the length of filaments within a single flower?
options: No, the length of filaments is always the same within a flower
Yes, there can be a variation in the length of filaments
It depends on the flower species
It depends on the type of stamen
122752.sol: Stamens of flower may be united with other members such as petals or among themselves. When stamens are attached to the petals, they are epipetalous as in brinjal, or epiphyllous when attached to the perianth as in the flowers of lily. The stamens in a flower may either remain free (polyandrous) or may be united in varying degrees. The stamens may be united into one bunch or one bundle (monoadelphous) as in china rose, or two bundles (diadelphous) as in pea, or into more than two bundles (polyadelphous) as in citru

123897.subject: Botany
123897.text: An animal cell with a diploid chromosome number of 2n = 16 is undergoing mitosis. What will be the number of chromosomes and chromatids respectively in this cell during Metaphase and Anaphase?
options: Metaphase: 16 chromosomes, 32 chromatids; Anaphase: 32 chromosomes, 32 chromatids
Metaphase: 16 chromosomes, 16 chromatids; Anaphase: 32 chromosomes, 32 chromatids
Metaphase: 16 chromosomes, 32 chromatids; Anaphase: 16 chromosomes, 32 chromatids
Metaphase: 32 chromosomes, 32 chromatids; Anaphase: 16 chromosomes, 16 chromatids
123897.sol: In a cell with 2n = 16 , the DNA replicates during the S phase, but the chromosome number remains the same. Each chromosome now consists of two sister chromatids. During Metaphase, the chromosomes align at the equator. The centromeres have not yet split. Therefore, there are 16 chromosomes, and since each has two chromatids, there are 16 2 = 32 chromatids. During Anaphase, the centromere of each chromosome splits. The 32 sister chromatids separate and are now referred to as daughter chromosomes. Because they are no

124554.subject: Botany
124554.text: What effect did the volatile substance released from ripened oranges have on unripened bananas?
124554.sol: Cousins confirmed the release of a volatile substance from ripened oranges that hastened the ripening of stored unripened bananas. Later this volatile substance was identified as ethylene, a gaseous PGR.

125147.subject: Botany
125147.text: What is the difference between glycolysis and fermentation?
options: Glycolysis produces pyruvic acid while fermentation produces lactic acid and ethanol
Glycolysis does not produce ATP while fermentation forms two ATP
125147.sol: The difference between glycolysis and fermentation is that Glycolysis produces pyruvic acid while fermentation produces lactic acid and ethanol

125152.subject: Botany
125152.text: When a specific biomolecule is utilised as the primary respiratory substrate, the volume of carbon dioxide evolved is slightly less than the volume of oxygen consumed, yielding a Respiratory Quotient (RQ) of approximately 0.9. Identify the most likely substrate.
125152.sol: The Respiratory Quotient (RQ) is defined as the ratio of the volume of CO₂ evolved to the volume of O₂ consumed during respiration. According to NCERT, the RQ depends upon the type of respiratory substrate used during respiration. When carbohydrates are used as substrate and are completely oxidised, the RQ will be 1. When fats (like tripalmitin) are used in respiration, the RQ is less than 1 (approximately 0.7). When proteins are respiratory substrates, the ratio would be about 0.9. Therefore, an RQ of 0.9 correspo

125803.subject: Botany
125803.text: How does a typical microsporangium appear in a transverse section?
125803.sol: The bilobed nature of an anther is very distinct in the transverse section of the anther. The anther is a four-sided (tetragonal) structure consisting of four microsporangia located at the corners, two in each lobe. The microsporangia develop further and become pollen sacs. They extend longitudinally all through the length of an anther and are packed with pollen grains . Structure of microsporangium: In a transverse section, a typical microsporangium appears near circular in outline. It is generally surrounded by f

125872.subject: Botany
125872.text: What is the unique characteristic of xenogamy?
options: It brings genetically different types of pollen grains to the stigma
It is similar to autogamy genetically
It occurs only in night-blooming flowers
125872.sol: Geitonogamy -Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of another flower of the same plant. Although geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination involving a pollinating agent, genetically it is similar to autogamy since the pollen grains come from the same plant. Xenogamy –Transfer of pollen grains from anther to the stigma of a different plant. This is the only type of pollination which during pollination brings genetically different types of pollen grains to the stigma.

126204.subject: Botany
126204.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding the reproductive features of plants. List-I List-II (A) Papaya (1) Prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy (B) Castor (2) Prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy (C) Commelina (3) Produces both chasmogamous and cleistogamous flowers Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
126204.sol: Papaya is a dioecious plant, meaning male and female flowers are present on different plants. This condition prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy. Thus, (A) matches with (2). Castor is a monoecious plant, where male and female flowers are borne on the same plant. This prevents autogamy (pollination within the same flower) but not geitonogamy (pollination between different flowers of the same plant). Thus, (B) matches with (1). Commelina produces two types of flowers: chasmogamous flowers (similar to flowers of ot

126269.subject: Botany
126269.text: During a field study, a researcher observes a pollinating agent transferring pollen between two distinct, open flowers. Later, genetic analysis of the resulting seeds reveals that they are genetically identical to the parent plant. Which of the following types of pollination has occurred in this scenario?
126269.sol: The observation that pollen transfer occurred between two distinct flowers via a pollinating agent indicates functional cross-pollination. This rules out normal autogamy (which occurs within the same flower) and cleistogamy (which occurs in closed flowers that do not open at all). The genetic analysis shows that the seeds are genetically identical to the parent plant. This means the pollen must have come from the same plant, ruling out xenogamy, which involves the transfer of pollen from a different plant and bring

126308.subject: Botany
126308.text: Assertion : Parthenocarpy involves formation of seedless fruits. Reason : Apomixis occurs without fertilisation.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
126308.sol: Production and development of seedless fruits is called parthenocarpy. It is of two types, vegetative and stimulative. Apomixis is a mode of reproduction which does not involve formation of zygote through gametic fusion. It is, therefore, akin to asexual reproduction. In plants apomixis commonly mimics sexual reproduction but produce seeds without fertilisation e.g., some species of Asteraceae and grasses.

126344.subject: Botany
126344.text: Hardest substance in plant kingdom is
126344.sol: Sporopollenin is the hardest substance in plant kingdom. It is the major constituent of outer layer (exine) of pollen grains. It is the most resistant organic material that can withstand high temperature as well as strong acids and alkali. No enzyme is known which can degrade it.

126460.subject: Botany
126460.text: What type of elements are found in the ash?
126460.sol: One weighs a small amount of a living tissue (say a leaf or liver and this is called wet weight) and dry it. All the water, evaporates. The remaining material gives dry weight. Now if the tissue is fully burnt, all the carbon compounds are oxidised to gaseous form (CO2, water vapour) and are removed. What is remaining is called ‘ash’. This ash contains inorganic elements (like calcium, magnesium etc). Inorganic compounds like sulphate, phosphate, etc., are also seen in the acid-soluble fraction.

127276.subject: Botany
127276.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: India is one of the 12 mega diversity countries of the world. Reason: Although India has only 2.4 per cent of the world’s land area, its share of the global species diversity is an impressive 8.1 per cent.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
127276.sol: Although India has only 2.4 per cent of the world’s land area, its share of the global species diversity is an impressive 8.1 per cent. That is what makes our country one of the 12 mega diversity countries of the world.

127457.subject: Botany
127457.text: Which one of the following is not a method of in situ conservation of biodiversity?
127457.sol: The approach of in situ conservation is the protection of threatened species in their natural habitat. Such methods of conservation include biosphere reserves, national parks, wildlife sanctuaries and sacred groves. Conservation of species in a special setting away from their natural habitat is called ex situ conservation. These include zoological parks, botanical gardens, wildlife safari parks, cryopreservation, etc.

127733.subject: Botany
127733.text: Decomposition Process Description A. Fragmentation 1. Formation of humus B. Leaching 2. Breaking down detritus into smaller particles C. Catabolism 3. Conversion of detritus into simpler inorganic substances D. Humification 4. Water-soluble nutrients are precipitated as unavailable salts
127733.sol: Fragmentation (A) is the breaking down of detritus into smaller particles (2). Leaching (B) involves water-soluble nutrients being precipitated as unavailable salts (4). Catabolism (C) is the conversion of detritus into simpler inorganic substances (3). Humification (D) is the formation of humus (1).

127797.subject: Botany
127797.text: Consider the following aquatic food chain: Phytoplankton Zooplankton Small fishes Large fishes Which of the given organisms represents the primary consumer in this ecosystem?
127797.sol: In an aquatic ecosystem, phytoplankton are the primary producers occupying the first trophic level. Zooplankton feed directly on phytoplankton, making them the primary consumers at the second trophic level. Small fishes and large fishes act as secondary and tertiary consumers, respectively. Answer: Zooplankton

128447.subject: Zoology
128447.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of steroid hormones called glucocorticoids from the adrenal medulla Reason: LH and FSH stimulate gonadal activity and hence are called gonadocorticoids
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
128447.sol: ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of steroid hormones called glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex. LH and FSH stimulate gonadal activity and hence are called gonadotrophins

128881.subject: Zoology
128881.text: What is the purpose of atrial systole in the heart?
options: To increase the flow of blood into the ventricles
To stimulate the ventricular muscles to contract
128881.sol: The ventricles now relax (ventricular diastole) and the ventricular pressure falls causing the closure of semilunar valves which prevents the backflow of blood into the ventricles. As the ventricular pressure declines further, the tricuspid and bicuspid valves are pushed open by the pressure in the atria exerted by the blood which was being emptied into them by the veins. The blood now once again moves freely to the ventricles. The ventricles and atria are now again in a relaxed (joint diastole) state, as earlier.

129353.subject: Zoology
129353.text: Match List I with List II: List I List II A. Fovea I. Visible coloured portion of eye that regulates diameter of pupil. B. Iris II. Point where optic nerve leaves the eyeball and photoreceptor cells are absent Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
129353.sol: Fovea At the posterior pole of the eye lateral to the blind spot, there is a yellowish pigmented spot called macula lutea with a central pit called the fovea. The fovea is a thinned-out portion of the retina where only the cones are densely packed. It is the point where the resolution is the greatest. Iris The continuation of the ciliary body forward to form a pigmented and opaque structure called the iris which is the visible coloured portion of the eye. Blind spot The optic nerves leave the eye and the retinal bl

129630.subject: Zoology
129630.text: Component of Urine Source A. Urea 1. Muscle metabolism B. Creatinine 2. Protein metabolism C. Uric Acid 3. Purine metabolism D. Ammonia 4. Deamination of amino acids
129630.sol: Urea comes from protein metabolism. Creatinine is a product of muscle metabolism. Uric Acid is a result of purine metabolism. Ammonia is formed by the deamination of amino acids.

129999.subject: Zoology
129999.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Residual volume is the volume of air that will remain in lungs after normal expiration 2. Functional residual capacity is the volume of air remaining after a forcible expiration 3. Expiratory capacity is the maximum volume of air a person can breathe in after a forced expiration 4. Total lung capacity is the maximum volume of air a person can breathe i
129999.sol: Residual Volume (RV): Volume of air remaining in the lungs even after a forcible expiration. This averages 1100 mL to 1200 mL.

132947.subject: Zoology
132947.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Flippers of penguins and dolphins are considered homologous structures. Reason (R): They have different anatomical origins but evolved to perform similar functions due to convergent evolution. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
132947.sol: The Assertion is false because the flippers of penguins (birds) and dolphins (mammals) are analogous structures, not homologous. They do not share a common ancestor with these specific flipper structures. The Reason is true. 133029.subject: Zoology
133029.text: Crocodile and penguin are similar to whale and dogfish in which one of the following features?
options: possess a solid single-stranded central nervous system
lay eggs and guard them till they hatch
have gill slits at some stage
133029.sol: Crocodile, penguin, whale and dogfish, all are chordates. So, all of these have gill slits at some stage of development.

133196.subject: Zoology
133196.text: What is the role of biotechnology in making vaccines available?
133196.sol: The advancements made in biological science have armed us to effectively deal with many infectious diseases and the use of vaccines and immunization programs have enabled us to completely eradicate a deadly disease like smallpox.. Biotechnology is at the verge of making available newer and safer vaccines. 133608.subject: Zoology
133608.text: Pebrine in silkworms is caused by
133608.sol: Pebrine or pepper disease is caused by protozoan Nosema bombycis. The parasite infects eggs and is therefore, transmitted to next generation. It kills caterpillars.

133649.subject: Zoology
133649.sol: Wuchereria bancrofii is a dreaded human parasite. It is digenetic parasite completing its life cycle in two hosts, the final host is man harbouring the adult worm. The adult worms live coiled up in the gland and lymph vessels of man.

133788.subject: Zoology
options: The use of chemicals to control plant diseases and pests
The use of biological methods for controlling plant diseases and pests
The use of technology for controlling plant diseases and pests
The use of artificial methods for controlling plant diseases and pests
133788.sol: Biocontrol refers to the use of biological methods for controlling plant diseases and pests. In modern society, these problems have been tackled increasingly by the use of chemicals – by use of insecticides and pesticides. These chemicals are toxic and extremely harmful, to human beings and animals alike, and have been polluting our environment (soil, ground water), fruits, vegetables and crop plants. Our soil is also polluted through our use of weedicides to remove weeds.
